segments.line: That first night is the darkest one you've ever seen.
A full Moon lights up the ground about a hundred times brighter than starlight alone.
Without it, every night is a moonless night. Forever.
And honestly? It's beautiful.
Out past the edge of town, the Milky Way spills across the sky like somebody knocked over a jar of glitter.
Astronomers are having the best week of their lives.
Mo sets up the telescope in your backyard and charges the neighbors a dollar a look.
By midnight, he's made forty- three dollars.
Mrs. Alvarez from next door sees Saturn's rings for the first time in her life and starts crying.
Mo gives her a refund. Then he charges her husband double.
Online, it's chaos. Hashtag where is the Moon is trending in every country.
Somebody sells a jar of 'genuine moonlight' for ten thousand dollars.
A werewolf fan club announces that it is officially shutting down.
There will never be another total solar eclipse.
No more Moon landings, either. The rockets being built to go back there suddenly have nowhere to go.
And your teacher points out something weird.
The word 'month' comes from the Moon. So does 'Monday'.
Every calendar on Earth was built around a thing that isn't there anymore.
Ellie is not having fun. She lies on the trampoline, staring at the empty spot in the sky.
'But what does the Moon actually do? ' she asks.
You don't have an answer. Not yet.
The next morning, Mo calls you at six.
'You need to come down to the harbor, ' he says.
'Grandpa's boat is stuck in the mud. '
